description: We are a team of six students in Medicine, Physical Therapy, CS, and Nursing—combining science, tech, and human-centered thinking. Passionate about space, coding, design, and storytelling, we aim for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to create a meaningful project that brings forgotten space missions and equipment back to life through creative narrative.
summary:
Project Summary
​Project Name: Legacy Pioneer
Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars
​What we developed:
Legacy Pioneer is an interactive educational ecosystem combining physical collectible cards and a simplified gaming experience. It brings NASA's historical space missions—such as deep space probes, Martian rovers, and lunar modules—back to life for space enthusiasts and children.
​How it addresses the challenge:
The project transforms complex archival data from NASA (NSSDCA) into engaging, easy-to-understand stories categorized into four unique themes: The Pioneers, The Survivors, The Discoverers, and The Silent Legends. Each card features key mission details, simplified scientific discoveries, final resting statuses, and interactive QR codes linked to rich digital content.
​Why it is important:
By turning discarded space equipment into engaging storytelling cards, Legacy Pioneer preserves space heritage, sparks children's curiosity, and makes aerospace science accessible, educational, and fun for the next generation of explorers.
details: SPACE LEGACY is an interactive 3D educational space exploration experience that takes users on a journey through the history of space exploration. The project combines a spaceship journey with immersive 3D environments where users can explore historical space missions and the technologies behind them. Users begin their journey from Earth and travel to the Moon and Mars. By selecting a destination, they can enter an interactive exploration environment, discover historical spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments, and interact with 3D representations of these technologies. Selecting a piece of hardware reveals its mission history, purpose, discoveries, current status, and contribution to space exploration. The project also includes a Deep Space section featuring important missions that explored asteroids, distant planets, and the wider universe. Benefits and Intended Impact: SPACE LEGACY aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable, especially for students and young learners. Instead of presenting space missions through static text and images, it allows users to explore space technology through interactive 3D experiences. The project helps users understand how different spacecraft and scientific instruments work, why they were developed, and how they contributed to our understanding of the Moon, Mars, and the universe. Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, support informal STEM education, and inspire the next generation to explore science, engineering, and space technology. Technologies and Tools: The project was developed using React 19, JavaScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three Drei, and CSS. These technologies enable interactive 3D environments, animated planetary scenes, spacecraft movement, camera transitions, and interactive hardware exploration. NASA mission information and publicly available space exploration resources are used to build the educational content and connect users with the history of real missions. Creativity and Innovation: The creative aspect of SPACE LEGACY is its combination of two experiences: a cinematic journey through space and an interactive hardware museum. Users do not simply read about historical missions; they travel to destinations and explore the technologies associated with them in immersive 3D environments. The experience connects the history of space exploration with the actual hardware used to achieve scientific discoveries. Design Considerations: The team considered educational accuracy, accessibility, usability, responsive design, realistic visual representation, and smooth navigation. Particular attention was given to making complex scientific information easy to understand while preserving the historical and scientific significance of each mission. The project is designed to provide an engaging educational experience across different screen sizes and devices.
